description: Click at an x,y POINT instead of at an element — for applications that draw their interface inside a canvas, where there is nothing to name: Figma, Miro, maps, charts, diagram and image editors. Everywhere else use qa_click: it names what it pressed, survives a re-render and tells you when it missed, none of which a coordinate can do. Coordinates are CSS pixels from the top-left of the VIEWPORT, not of the page — the same frame a qa_screenshot is taken in, so reading a position off a screenshot works; scroll the target into view first. The reply names the element the browser found under the point, and carries the usual `changed` diff, so you can tell a press that did something from one that landed on empty canvas. HONEST LIMIT, and it is not theoretical: these events carry `isTrusted: false`. Anything that checks it will ignore the click and say nothing — measured on npmjs, where a React checkbox took the synthetic click and reverted it on the next render while a real one held. Canvas applications do not check it, which is why this verb is for them. When a page does check it, the reply carries `realMouse`: how to press the same point with a real click from the operating system (cliclick on macOS, PowerShell or AutoHotkey on Windows, xdotool on Linux) and how to turn this point into a screen one. Requires the one-time “Agent control” confirmation in the panel; without it the extension answers consent-required and does nothing.

tabId.description: Target tab (from qa_tabs); omit for the active tab

x.description: CSS pixels from the LEFT of the viewport

y.description: CSS pixels from the TOP of the viewport

name: qa_click_point
title: Click a point on a canvas
